name: secure-random
summary: Cryptographically-secure randomness (dice, integers, floats, shuffling, passwords, tokens, UUIDs, weighted picks) exposed as an MCP server, plus chi-square tests to prove the output isn't biased.
problem: Language models cannot generate genuine randomness: they predict a plausible-looking token rather than sampling one, so 'pick a random number' reliably comes back skewed toward whatever value is most common in training data -- the well-documented '27 phenomenon', where several major assistants asked for a random number 1-50 all answered 27.
